series_label: People using at least basic drinking water services (% of population)
source_or_custodian: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (washdata.org); organizations WHO and UNICEF; published via World Bank World Development Indicators (WB_WDI)
release_or_vintage: WDI version date 2026-07-01; JMP source publication date 2025-08-25 (accessed 2025-09-30); release calendar: every odd year in September
status_or_notes: No 2025 value is available. Server coverage is 2000-2024. The values are JMP modelled estimates: the JMP fits a linear regression to national survey, census and administrative data, with rules for interpolation and extrapolation. No observation status flags were returned.
definition: The percentage of people using at least basic water services. This indicator encompasses both people using basic water services as well as those using safely managed water services. Basic drinking water services is defined as drinking water from an improved source, provided collection time is not more than 30 minutes for a round trip. Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.
